speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; it's quite extensive. To start, have you experienced any episodes of double vision, drooping eyelids, or slurred speech in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying that; the "drunken" gait and unilateral clumsiness suggest a progressive neurological issue. Have you noticed any changes in your vision, swallowing difficulties, or muscle weakness in other areas? Also, how many years ago was your last significant medical event or hospitalization?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a crucial piece of information; given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, we must urgently assess for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). Did you experience any new visual disturbances, such as blind spots or loss of color vision, alongside your gait issues?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of Progressive Multifocal Leucoencephalopathy (PML).

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Patient
text: The walking difficulty and coordination problems are the main issues. I do not have chest pain or other major symptoms besides the neurological problems. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.
